assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Each policy threshold (650 for non-seniors, 600 for seniors) is verifiable from the table via boundary rows or a dedicated column.
assertions.evidence: 'At the standard threshold, not above it | 40 | 650 ... REJECTED' beside 'Just above the standard threshold | 40 | 651 ... APPROVED', and similarly '70 | 600 ... REJECTED' / '70 | 601 ... APPROVED'

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms, not abstract codes.
assertions.evidence: '40 | 650 | true | REJECTED', '651 | ... | APPROVED' — concrete ages, scores, and enum outcomes throughout

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario"

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'Just above the standard threshold', 'Senior age boundary, lower threshold applies', 'Qualifying score with missing income information' — all condition-phrased

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language.
assertions.evidence: Header row: 'Scenario | Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Result?'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Result?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 1 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 1 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Distinct concerns are each covered without a monolithic cross-multiplied table.
assertions.evidence: Single table with rows grouped by concern (threshold pairs, age boundary, income variations, precedence) rather than a full cartesian product of age x score x income

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules.
assertions.evidence: 11 rows including redundant extras like 'Senior qualifying score with missing income information | 70 | 610 | | PENDING_REVIEW' and both 'Below threshold rejects regardless of stable income' (value-set) plus a separate null-income row at the same score 500, re-proving the same precedence rule multiple times

assertions.text: Age boundary, credit score categorisation, and income status are each covered.
assertions.evidence: Age: rows '64|610|true|REJECTED' vs '65|610|true|APPROVED'; Credit: '650...REJECTED' vs '651...APPROVED'; Income: '700|false|REJECTED' vs '700||PENDING_REVIEW'

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description do not restate values the table already shows.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'approved above a credit score of 650' and 'senior applicants (age 65+) ... lower threshold of 600' and 'senior age cutoff is inclusive at 65' — restating the exact 650/600/65 values already shown as row cells (e.g. Age=65, Credit Score=650/600)

assertions.text: Effect of stable income visible from table rows holding score and age constant.
assertions.evidence: Rows 'Qualifying score with unstable income | 40 | 700 | false | REJECTED' vs 'Qualifying score with missing income information | 40 | 700 | | PENDING_REVIEW' — same age/score, differing income, differing decision

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Result column varies across REJECTED/APPROVED/PENDING_REVIEW and none of the expectation cells are verbatim copies of Age/Credit Score/Stable Income input values

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Boundary rows like '650|true|REJECTED' vs '651|true|APPROVED' and '600|true|REJECTED' vs '601|true|APPROVED' make thresholds inferable; scenario names and columns fully describe the operation; assertEquals only checks equality with the Result? column, no hidden criteria.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or the method name it falls back to) states what the code under test does.
assertions.evidence: void evaluatesLoanApproval(...) — the method name describes the SUT's action (evaluating loan approval), not a restated domain fact.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, held constant across rows, must be visible as a column or named in the title/description.
assertions.evidence: All outcome-relevant values (Age, Credit Score, Stable Income) are explicit columns; thresholds (650, 600, 65) are additionally stated in the @Description, so nothing decision-relevant is hidden in the method body or a field.
